_authority: Owner, 2026-10-15 (L48, 2.25.0): 'my main task is to level up pedagogy - bloom taxonomy needs to be on higher level. thats why we have tablets ... before that we used google docs/google classroom tasks, now we have tablets, so we can use all of their functionality to lift bloom taxonomy/pedagogy level up'. The Bloom map: what level each ILO asks for, what level each task reaches, where a task sits below its ILO, and which tablet task type would lift it. Read by scripts/bloom_map.py (and through it make_architecture_page.py and content_script.py); the judgement a list cannot make is in bloom/GUIDE.md. The revised taxonomy (Anderson & Krathwohl, 2001). Every floor here is a SUGGESTION in 2.25.0 - shown, never blocking.

means.en: recall a fact, a name, a number
explain it in own words, sort it, compare it
do it - operate, set, measure, carry out the procedure
means.lv: izdarīt - darbināt, iestatīt, izmērīt, veikt procedūru
means.ru: сделать - управлять, установить, измерить, выполнить процедуру

means.en: find the cause, the fault, the hazard in a real situation
means.lv: atrast cēloni, kļūmi, bīstamību reālā situācijā
means.ru: найти причину, неисправность, опасность в реальной ситуации

examples.en: find the cause of, diagnose, distinguish

means.en: decide what to do and say why; judge someone's decision
means.lv: izlemt, ko darīt, un pamatot; izvērtēt kāda lēmumu
means.ru: решить, что делать, и обосновать; оценить чужое решение

means.en: make a plan, a procedure, a checklist of their own

verbs._how: How the level of an ILO is read. en: whole words, the script adds -s, -es, -ed, -ing (identify -> identifies, identified). lv and ru: word STEMS - anything that starts with the stem matches (aprakst -> apraksta, aprakstīt). Multi-word entries are phrases. An entry ending in $ is a whole word only (lv 'veic$' - so that 'veicināt', to promote, is not read as 'veikt', to carry out). The ILO's level is the HIGHEST of the verbs that lead a clause - the first verb, and any verb straight after a comma, a semicolon or a lead word (and, or, to; un, spēj; и, уметь) - so a noun deep in the object is not read as a verb. 'weak' verbs cannot be observed or measured: they get a level, and a note. A verb in more than one level in real use (select, determine, check, определить) is left OUT on purpose - the report says 'not in the list' and Claude judges it (bloom/GUIDE.md 2). A starting list: add the verbs your programmes use.

weak._why: These say what happens inside a head - nobody can watch a trainee 'know'. A programme's Main ILO keeps them (verbatim, L2); a Sub-ILO is re-expressed with a verb that can be watched, the operator approving (status re-expressed). STCW's own column 'knowledge, understanding and proficiency' is written this way - the level is still read from it.

lead_words._why: A verb straight after one of these leads a clause: 'and describe', 'to operate', 'spēj aprakstīt', 'уметь применять'.

mechanics._how: The level a tablet task type USUALLY reaches (typical), and the highest it CAN reach when it is written for it (ceiling) - with how. A question may state its own level ('bloom': 4, 'bloom_why': '...') when it is written above the usual; it is then shown as stated, and a stated level above the ceiling is pointed out. Create (6) is reached only by 'build the plan', written for it (2.28.0) - and in a narrow sense: the trainee composes a plan from given cards. Real creation stays with the practical exercise.

single_choice.higher: give a short real situation, and make the right option one that has to be worked out from it - not a fact recalled

multi_select.higher: a situation with several clues; the trainee picks every clue that points to the fault

cloze.higher: gaps that carry the reasoning (because ... so ...) rather than the facts

match.higher: match each situation to the action it needs, not a term to its definition

categorise.higher: sort observed symptoms into the causes behind them

order.higher: order the steps of a procedure the trainee will actually carry out, with the situation given

hotspot.higher: tap where you would act - the valve to close, the point to measure - not just where a part is

label_diagram.higher: label what each part does, not only its name

read_instrument.higher: read it, then say what the reading means for the operation

scenario.higher: at each step the trainee chooses the action AND the reason, and sees the consequence of a wrong one

build_the_plan.higher: give the situation the plan must fit, and cards from more than one procedure, so the trainee composes the plan for it

timeline.higher: ask where it should have been stopped, and why - the feedback names the barrier that failed

true_false.higher: Part A - statements that state a reason ("... because ..."), not a bare fact

calculate.higher: give more data than is needed, so the trainee has to choose what applies

investigate.higher: add a source that rules out the tempting wrong conclusion, so the trainee has to weigh the evidence

take_apart.higher: ask what a part does from where it sits, then operate it

test_atmosphere.higher: follow it with the entry decision as its own question

floors._apply_plus: A suggestion, not a rule (2.25.0): at least half of a module's self-check and module-check questions at Apply or higher. On paper and in Google Classroom almost everything was Remember; the tablet can let the trainee operate, find and decide.
floors._reaches: A suggestion, not a rule (2.25.0): for every Sub-ILO the module check has at least one question at the Sub-ILO's level or higher - otherwise the module never checks what it promised.
